question: An engineer holds only an Admin API key (no org:admin OAuth token) and has a checklist of tasks to finish before an audit deadline this afternoon. Based on which endpoints accept an Admin API key, which of the following tasks can they complete using just that key? (Select all that apply.)
options: A) Register a new federation issuer for a Kubernetes cluster the team just provisioned.
B) Retrieve basic organization information via the /v1/organizations/me endpoint.
C) Create a new service account for an upcoming CI workload.
D) List the organization's existing API keys and inspect each one's expiration status.
E) Remove an organization member whose role is currently set to admin.
F) Add a specific user as a member of one workspace with a given workspace role.
correct_answers: B) Retrieve basic organization information via the /v1/organizations/me endpoint.
D) List the organization's existing API keys and inspect each one's expiration status.
F) Add a specific user as a member of one workspace with a given workspace role.
explanations: Incorrect as an Admin-API-key-only task. Federation issuer endpoints require an org:admin OAuth token; Admin API keys are explicitly not accepted there.
Correct. The organization info endpoint example explicitly shows successful authentication with an Admin API key via x-api-key.
Incorrect as an Admin-API-key-only task. Service account endpoints require an org:admin OAuth token, the same carve-out that applies to federation issuers and rules.
Correct. Listing API keys is a standard Admin API endpoint that accepts the x-api-key header with an Admin API key.
Incorrect as an Admin-API-key-only task. Organization members with the admin role cannot be removed through the API at all, regardless of which credential authenticates the call.
Correct. Adding or updating workspace members is documented as usable with an Admin API key via x-api-key, no OAuth token required.
